chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Ja'far (peace be upon him) and his son Ali (peace be upon him) was in his lap. He was kissing him, sucking his tongue, placing him on his shoulder, and hugging him close, while saying: 'May my father and mother be your ransom! How sweet is your scent, how pure your nature, and how clear is your excellence!' I said: 'May I be your ransom, by God, a feeling of love for this child has settled in my heart that has not settled for anyone else but you.' He said to me: 'O Mufaddal, he is to me as I was to my father (peace be upon him), [as God said:] Offspring, one of the other. And God heareth and knoweth all things.' I said: 'Is he the master of this affair after you?' He said: 'Yes. Whoever obeys him will make progress, and whoever disobeys him is an infidel.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَتِي: In the same position/status as me

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq say about the status of his son Ali ibn Musa after him?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the physical affection and spiritual status of Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) as the designated successor, with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly linking his authority to that of his father. The Imam’s declaration that 'obedience is guidance and disobedience is disbelief' underscores the Shia doctrine of *Ismah* and the necessity of following the Imam's authority for salvation. The reference to 'offspring of one another' reinforces the continuous lineage of Imams, a key concept in Shia genealogy and theology.
